summary: Per-frame wheel ground-contact physics step: computes per-wheel track grip (either a uniform copy or a position-projected 1D-table lookup), queries the spatial grid for the body ground plane, generates collision contacts and friction response for 4 wheels, resolves ground penetration into angular-momentum impulses plus a per-frame impact packet, and optionally applies a per-wheel contact impulse loop gated by a suspension flag.

local_names.this: vehicle physics object: body transform pointer 0x15F0, wheel contact arrays 0x1660/0x1668, hit-result pointer array 0x16E0, penetration array 0x16F0, grip array 0x4FC, physics-state container pointer 0x1F00, spatial-grid query results 0x1904..0x1928
local_names.v53: projected lateral-bias value used by the per-wheel grip lookup
local_names.v77_v83: SpatialGridQuery input struct assembled from body world position plus constant double bit patterns
local_names.v56: spatial-grid hit object: reads surface fields at +20/+24/+36/+44
local_names.result: suspension flag byte at this+0x1724 that gates the final impulse loop

operations.description: Branch on the float constants flt_8AFEEC and flt_8AFEE8: when equal, fill all wheel grips with the uniform value; otherwise compute a per-wheel projected grip.
Uniform-grip path: fill the 4 wheel grip doubles at this+0x4FC (8-byte slots, 1124-byte stride) with flt_8AFEE8.

Per-wheel grip path: for each of 4 wheels, sample wheel state via PositionChangeMonitor on *(this+0x1F00)+12, compute the absolute lateral deviation (dot product of wheel position against the lookup basis minus the projected bias), pass it through F_1DTableLookupWithLerp and store the absolute value into the grip slot at this+0x4FC.
Body ground-query path is gated by the contact-active pointer at *(this+0x1F00)+0xCD4 being non-null together with the post-processing flag byte at +0xD14 being set.
Ground-query path: Matrix3x3VectorMultiply(body rotation at *(this+0x15F0)+0x1C, world position input, output at this+0x1918) rotates the body position into world space.

Assemble the body query vector (v58/v59/v60) from world-position doubles at this+0x1918/0x1920/0x1928 offset by the body-origin translation at *(this+0x15F0)+0x4 and a 0.15 raise, then build the SpatialGridQuery input struct v77..v83 carrying the constant double bit patterns 1717986918, 1071015526, 0x40000000, 1201543096.
Ground-query path: SpatialGridQuery(&v77) queries the spatial grid; the returned surface pointer is stored to this+0x1904.
On a ground hit store the ground height this+0x1908 = v59 - v84; otherwise fall back to this+0x1908 = this+0x1910 and this+0x190C = this+0x1914.
For each of 4 wheels: CollisionContactGenerationAndFrictionResponse on the wheel contact struct at this+0x28C (1124-byte stride) with the per-frame time step double at this+0x60.

Wheel contact loop: for each of 4 wheels, TransformApply3D(body rotation at *(this+0x15F0)+0x1C, body origin at +0x4, wheel contact point array this+0x1660, output &v58), then run SpatialGridQuery and store the returned surface pointer into the wheel hit-result pointer array at this+0x16E0.
Store the per-wheel ground separation double into the penetration array at this+0x16F0; when dword_7CE958 (tire-model mode flag) is set, the value is biased by 0.01.

If the computed separation at this+0x16F0 is negative (wheel penetrating the ground): set the ground-contact flag byte at this+0x1718 to 1, build the penetration vector from the wheel contact point (this+0x1660 world position) minus the body position, derive the contact plane normal from the hit-result surface array at this+0x16E0, and compute the impulse scalar v64 = -385000*separation - 17500*slip term.
AccumulateAngularMomentum(&v74, v92) applies the ground-contact angular-momentum impulse at the wheel contact point.

When the impulse v64 exceeds the previous maximum at this+0x171C and the hit surface allows impulse recording (byte at hit+44): update this+0x171C = v64, compute a clamped strength v57 (capped at 1.0) and a clamped distance v36 (capped at 2.0), and write the contact packet into the physics-state container: magnitude compared against *(this+0x1F00)+0xB0, strength and response written to +0xB8/+0xBC, and the wheel world position to +0xC0.
The final per-wheel contact impulse loop runs only when the suspension/contact flag byte at this+0x1724 is non-zero.

Final impulse loop: for each of 4 wheels, transform the contact offsets at this+0x1668 (stride 3 doubles, reading the adjacent elements this+0x1660 and this+0x1670) into world space using the body transform matrix at *(this+0x15F0) (translation elements +0x4/+0xC/+0x14, rotation elements +0x24..+0x5C, and impulse terms +0x64..+0x8C), subtract the body position, build the impulse vector from 160000*offset - 6500*velocity terms (velocity read from this+0x1748/0x1750/0x1758), and feed it to AccumulateAngularMomentum(&v58, v91).
Invoked from the frame-path integration step PhysicsIntegrationStep (00441D60).

unresolved: The 15 read-only constant globals (dbl_59E420, dbl_59E430, flt_59E43C, flt_59E800, dbl_59E880, dbl_59EB20, dbl_59EC60, dbl_59ED80, dbl_59ED88, dbl_59ED90, dbl_59ED98, dbl_59EDA0, dbl_59EDA8, dbl_7C9360, unk_8AFEC0) are read but their exact consumption as inlined literals (for example 0.15, 385000, 17500, 6500, 160000) was not deterministically recovered from the packet; the fill's DERIVED names for them are prose, not evidence.

The wheel hit surface reads at hit-object offsets +20/+24/+36/+44 and the contact struct at this+0x28C are derived from the raw source dereferences; their exact struct roles are not independently confirmed.

Whether the fill's naming of this+0x1660/0x1668/0x1670 as suspension constants is correct is doubtful: the raw source shows them as the wheel world-space contact point output of TransformApply3D, which is the reading adopted here.
